Hi Clara — thanks for the redlines and the clear questions. I looped in Ben (ops) and Laura (security) so we can give a thorough operational walkthrough.

High level answers up front:
- Active service data: we run a three-stage erase (API delete -> KV cache purge -> physical wipe/garbage collection on storage layer). SLA for API-initiated customer erasure is configurable but default in our DPA is 30 days to complete all stages, with the API delete visible within minutes.
- Archived objects: archives are tiered; archived blobs are scheduled for a controlled purge. For standard DPA we quote 90 days for archive purge; for onshore-only retention scenarios we can propose a separate 30/60/90 timeline depending on contractual needs.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are handled via a separate retention/exclusion policy. Some backups are immutable for a fixed TTL; deletion of those entries requires an evidence-backed purge action that we can schedule.

Ben and Laura — can you prepare a short runbook and a sample audit trail for the demo? Clara asked for the week of Jan 24–26 morning PST; propose Jan 25 at 10:00 PST.

Hi Clara & team — adding more detail for the call and answering the two items below. I'll be the primary ops presenter on Jan 25.

Snapshot/backups scope
- Crash-consistent snapshots: stored in region-local block storage and referenced in our backup manifest. By default snapshots inherit the tenant retention policy; we treat them as separate retention groups (live, archive, backup).
- Onshore copies: for customers that require onshore-only processing we maintain a geo-replicated onshore snapshot. That copy is tagged and managed by our geo-fencing controller and is subject to a separate purge workflow.

Purge process (simplified)
1) Customer initiates erase request via API or support ticket.
2) Erase orchestration runs: marks object as logically deleted, enqueues background workers to clear KV and cache, and creates an Erase Job ID.
3) Storage GC: background garbage collection removes blobs from primary stores.
4) Archive purge: separate job that enumerates archived containers and issues delete operations; this is batched and can take up to the archive SLA window.
5) Backup purge: for immutable backups we register a backup purge ticket and schedule a purge window; for mutable backups the deletion is performed immediately by remove operations.

Evidence and certification
- Every Erase Job emits an audit bundle: {job_id, initiator, timestamp, affected_containers[], status_history[]}. We keep these bundles in a tamper-evident audit store for the retention period.
- We can surface a human-readable "Erase Certificate" PDF on request that summarizes the job (job_id, timestamps, blobs removed, verification checks). Creating that certificate is part of our enterprise support package; we can include it for Acme under the contract or provide a runbook so your team can validate logs directly.

Operational SLAs we propose (defaults, negotiable)
- API-visible deletion: immediate (minutes).
- Complete service-level erase (active + cache + KV): 30 days.
- Archive purge (standard): 90 days; can be reduced to 30/60 for an additional operational commitment.
- Backup purge for immutable onshore backups: scheduled within 180 days unless otherwise agreed; acceleration options available under a paid support tier.
